headline: High-risk default interaction: Flowise can feed outputs into Open Interpreter, creating dangerous prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can ingest files and browser/HTTP tool outputs, and Open Interpreter can read the filesystem, use the clipboard, and execute code with user privileges. That creates a default path where attacker-controlled content from Flowise can be treated as instructions by Open Interpreter. The shared filesystem and broad egress make provenance weak.
conditions: IF Flowise writes untrusted content to a shared file or prompt buffer that Open Interpreter reads
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto-run or equivalent reduced-confirmation mode
mitigations: Disable shared filesystem handoff between the agents
Require manual review of every Flowise-generated prompt before Open Interpreter consumes it
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
Turn off Open Interpreter auto-run / confirmation bypass
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/data separation in the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, while Open Interpreter can access the entire local filesystem and clipboard. If Flowise forwards sensitive content into Open Interpreter, Open Interpreter can expose it through broad network egress or model-provider calls. The pair therefore has a realistic default leakage path across both agents.
conditions: IF Flowise receives secrets, customer data, or uploaded files
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to read those artifacts from the shared machine or clipboard
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Run Open Interpreter in a separate user account
Restrict outbound network access for Open Interpreter
Remove secrets from Flowise chatflows before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted write access to the same local machine surfaces: Flowise writes server filesystem state and Open Interpreter writes the user filesystem and can modify git state. Their concurrency models also share state differently, so simultaneous writes can collide without locking. This is a direct mutable-resource conflict in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, repo, or workspace
IF no external lock or serialization layer is configured
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Pause one agent while the other writes
Avoid letting Open Interpreter modify git state in shared repos
Use filesystem locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based orchestrator that can emit tool outputs, and Open Interpreter can act on code blocks and filesystem state. If Flowise output is passed to Open Interpreter without verification, errors or hallucinations can become executed actions, including shell commands or file edits. The pair therefore supports an unsafe default action chain.
conditions: IF Flowise-generated text is used as an instruction source for Open Interpreter
IF Open Interpreter confirmation is bypassed or the operator approves blindly
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require structured, schema-validated outputs from Flowise
Disable auto-run in Open Interpreter
Log and diff every proposed action before execution
requires-engineering: add policy checks that reject executable text

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine. If regulated data is routed from Flowise into Open Interpreter, the latter's broad local access and network egress can violate retention or residency expectations. The profiles do not specify a named certification mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in Flowise and then exposed to Open Interpreter
IF local-machine access includes data subject to retention or residency controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workflow
Use separate storage locations with distinct retention rules
Disable unnecessary logging in both agents
Restrict Open Interpreter network access
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling boundaries
